beats.en: Ravens are large black birds, and their voice is a rough croak, not a song. The book says even ravens croak, as frogs do. In stories, the fox is usually shown as the cunning animal.
beats.speakEn: Ravens are large black birds, and their voice is a rough croak, not a song. The book says even ravens croak, as frogs do. In stories, the fox is usually shown as the cunning animal.

beats.en: A raven is sitting on the branch of a tree, holding a small piece of food in his beak. The fox, whose name is Reynard, looks up at him hungrily. The fox would go far to get that food, so he does not ask for it.
beats.speakEn: A raven is sitting on the branch of a tree, holding a small piece of food in his beak. The fox, whose name is Reynard, looks up at him hungrily. The fox would go far to get that food, so he does not ask for it.

textbookBox.ref: CBSE Class 6 english · The Raven and the Fox · Deeper Textbook Ideas
textbookBox.concept: The raven does not see that the fox is joking. He forgets that his voice is only a croak. Filled with foolish pride, he opens his beak to sing, and the food drops down to the fox.

beats.en: The raven does not see that the fox is joking. He forgets that his voice is only a croak. Filled with foolish pride, he opens his beak to sing, and the food drops down to the fox.
beats.speakEn: The raven does not see that the fox is joking. He forgets that his voice is only a croak. Filled with foolish pride, he opens his beak to sing, and the food drops down to the fox.

beats.en: The fox laughs and tells the raven to ignore sweet words that only make you feel good. He adds that pride is unwise and that the raven has just got a surprising lesson. This is the moral of the fable.
beats.speakEn: The fox laughs and tells the raven to ignore sweet words that only make you feel good. He adds that pride is unwise and that the raven has just got a surprising lesson. This is the moral of the fable.

textbookBox.ref: CBSE Class 6 english · The Raven and the Fox · Complete Summary
textbookBox.concept: Perched means sat on something, here on a branch. A limb is a branch of a tree. A morsel is a small piece of food. To seek is to look for something. Eyed means looked at with interest.

beats.en: Let us review the key takeaway from The Raven and the Fox: Perched means sat on something, here on a branch. A limb is a branch of a tree. A morsel is a small piece of food. To seek is to look for something. Eyed means looked at with interest.
